call_points.text: FY27 growth guided above the 15% long-term target, but no specific number given.
EBITDA margin band of 9-10% reiterated for the year.
Price growth was 14% and volume growth 9% of the 23% blended growth.
South grew 36.7% and non-South 12%, attributed to summer weather differences.
Net cash stood at ₹670 Cr versus ₹155 Cr a year ago, helped by higher payables.
Payables are unusually high this quarter and expected to revert to normative levels.
Sunflame integration complete; NPD impact expected from Q2, with margin recovery slower than revenue.
Lighting to be launched this financial year; solar rooftop and BESS are the next growth areas.
Net cash rose to ₹231 Cr as of March 2026 from ₹64 Cr a year earlier; debt repayments are done.
Board recommended a final dividend of 150%, or ₹1.5 per equity share.
call_points.versus_prior: final dividend now recommended; shareholder approval still pending

call_points.text: West Asia war has caused commodity inflation and supply uncertainty; management calls the inflation trend severe.
Sulfuric acid is a controlled substance under government rationing; storage capacity is limited, though supplies are locked for over a month.
About ₹300-400 Cr spent over the last 8 years building manufacturing plants; the company is now fully integrated.
Lighting foray is still work in progress, expected to be brought to market in the early next quarter.
BLDC contributes roughly 40% of ceiling fan sales; BLDC chimneys launched, mixer grinders not yet.
Ending Q4 on a strong note, management sees indications of a supportive summer and a hopeful start to FY27.
Gross margin contracted by 20 bps YoY to 35.3% in Q4 FY26.

guidance.statement: Company strives to grow 10-12% in volume plus 1-2% price growth, culminating in 15% growth
At least 10% EBITDA margin expected in FY27, subject to inflation
FY27 revenue growth to be more than 15%
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 9-10%
Capex of ₹150-170 Cr per annum for the next two years
Ad spend at 2.5% of revenue for FY27

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Durables > Household Appliances

operating_notes.text: About 75% of the required 8-13% price hikes had been passed on as of the May 12 call, with the balance expected as high-cost inventory arrives in May-June.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor portfolio and is customer-linked, not category-linked.
BLDC contributes roughly 40% of ceiling fan sales; non-South markets were 48% of FY26 revenue.
Price growth was 14% and volume growth 9% of the 23% blended growth in Q1FY27.
South market revenue grew 36.7% YoY versus 12% for non-South, attributed to summer weather differences.
Payables rose because copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers (95% domestic vs 70-80% earlier) who give credit, which the CFO called a one-off.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,755.27 Cr (+14.1% YoY), net profit ₹112.13 Cr (+23.0% YoY).
On May 12, 2026, V-Guard Industries submitted its Q4 FY26 investor presentation reporting revenue of ₹1,755.27 Cr and PAT of ₹112.13 Cr.
On May 12, 2026, V-Guard Industries received a Customs Order-in-Original confirming a ₹0.68 Cr duty demand and an equal penalty for product misclassification spanning May 2020 to July 2024.
Vikas Kumar Tak, Director, announced the Q4-FY26 earnings call recording on May 12, 2026, available at the company’s website.
Vikas Kumar Tak, CFO of V-Guard Industries, corrected book closure to August 1–11, 2026, with dividend payable on July 31, 2026.

On May 18, 2026, V-Guard Industries filed the transcript of its May 12, 2026 Q4 and FY26 earnings call, where management guided to at least 10% FY27 EBITDA margin and 10-12% volume growth amid 8-13% input cost inflation.
Chittilappilly Thomas Kochouseph, Promoter, declared no encumbrance of shares by Promoter Group or PAC during FY ended March 31, 2026.
Q1FY27 (Jul 30, 2026): V-Guard reported revenue of ₹1,810 Cr (+23.5% YoY) and PAT of ₹130 Cr (+76%), with management guiding FY27 growth above 15% and capex of ₹150-170 Cr a year.
